extra.message: Sensitive Data Exposure - Debug Endpoint Reveals All Passwords Without Authentication — Any unauthenticated attacker can retrieve plaintext passwords, email addresses, and admin status for all users in the system. This enables complete account takeover of all users including the admin. [verified: Duplicate of finding [3]: same debug() endpoint at line 24-26 exposing all passwords without authentication, confirmed always-vulnerable by app.py comment.]

Excessive Data Exposure – Unauthenticated Debug Endpoint Reveals All User Passwords — Any unauthenticated attacker can retrieve all usernames, plaintext passwords, email addresses, and admin status for every user in the system, enabling complete account takeover. [verified: The debug() view at line 25 calls User.get_all_users_debug() which returns password+admin via json_debug() in user_model.py line 59; the OpenAPI spec declares /users/v1/_debug with NO security scheme, and app.py line 10 explicitly confirms this is always vulnerable regardless of the vuln flag.]

Mass Assignment – Self-Registration as Administrator — Any unauthenticated user can register an account with admin=True, then use admin privileges to delete other users, access all resources, and perform any administrative action. [verified: When vuln=1, register_user() directly honors attacker-supplied 'admin' key from JSON body (line 60); register_user_schema lacks 'admin' in properties and has no additionalProperties:false, so jsonschema passes it through. Any unauthenticated registrant gains admin=True with no compensating control.]

Broken Object Level Authorization – Unauthorized Password Change of Other Users — Any authenticated user can hijack any other user's account (including admin) by changing their password, leading to complete account takeover. [verified: When vuln=1, update_password() at line 187 uses the path parameter 'username' directly (User.query.filter_by(username=username)) instead of the JWT sub claim; the token is validated for presence only, allowing any authenticated user to overwrite any other user's password.]

IDOR in update_password allows any authenticated user to change another user's password — An authenticated attacker can change the password of any other user, including admins, leading to complete account takeover. [verified: Duplicate of finding [2]: same update_password() endpoint at line 187, same BOLA via path parameter username ignoring JWT sub, same account-takeover risk.]

Broken Object Level Authorization - password change for any user via path parameter — Account takeover: any authenticated user can change the password of any other user (including admin), gaining full access to that account. [verified: Duplicate of finding [2]: same BOLA in update_password() at line 187, same use of path parameter instead of JWT subject for target user resolution.]

Hardcoded Weak JWT Signing Secret Enables Token Forgery — An attacker can forge JWT tokens for any user (including admin) and gain unauthorized access to all authenticated endpoints, read any user's books with secrets, change any user's password, and delete users. [verified: Same hardcoded weak key at config.py:13 (reported as line 12, minor offset); encode_auth_token (user_model.py:39) and decode_auth_token (line 48) both use this static secret, enabling forged admin tokens with no compensating control.]

Hardcoded JWT Signing Secret Key — Attacker can forge valid JWT tokens for any user including admin, bypassing all authentication and gaining full access to protected endpoints. [verified: config.py line 13 hardcodes SECRET_KEY='random'; no os.getenv override exists for it (only 'vulnerable'/'tokentimetolive' are env-driven). This weak string is the HS256 JWT signing key (user_model.py:39,48), enabling trivial token forgery for any user including admin.]

Hardcoded weak JWT secret key enables token forgery — An attacker who learns the hardcoded secret can forge valid JWT tokens for any user, including admins, completely bypassing authentication. [verified: Same hardcoded string 'random' at config.py:13 used as HMAC key for all JWT tokens; no environment variable or config file can override it, and the 'vuln' flag does not gate this setting.]

SQL injection via raw string interpolation in get_user query — An unauthenticated attacker can execute arbitrary SQL on the SQLite database, extracting all data (including passwords), modifying records, or deleting the entire database. [verified: Same SQLi as finding 0: get_user() at line 72 constructs the query via f-string from the unsanitized path param, executed via text() on line 73, with no authentication or input validation on the endpoint.]

Broken Object Level Authorization – Unauthorized Book Secret Access — Any authenticated user can read the secret content of books belonging to other users, exposing confidential per-user data. [verified: When vuln=1 (default), get_by_title() at line 50-51 queries Book.query.filter_by(book_title=...) with NO ownership scoping after token validation succeeds; the user lookup via resp['sub'] is only executed in the vuln=0 branch. No middleware, decorator, or other control restricts access to the book owner.]

Missing ownership check allows any authenticated user to access any book's secret content — Unauthorized access to another user's private book data including the 'secret' content field. [verified: Same BOLA as finding 0: the vulnerable branch at line 51 skips user scoping entirely, so any authenticated bearer-token holder can retrieve any book's secret_content by title with no ownership check.]

Broken Object Level Authorization - any authenticated user can read any book secret — Data breach: any authenticated user can exfiltrate all book secrets across all users by iterating through known or guessed book titles. [verified: Same BOLA as findings 0 and 1: the query at line 51 (Book.query.filter_by(book_title=...)) has no user_id or user filter when vuln=1, exposing all books' secret_content to any authenticated attacker.]

Missing authentication on database initialization endpoint — Denial of service and data loss: attacker can repeatedly wipe the production database, destroying all user data and book records. [verified: Same issue as finding 0: the /createdb OpenAPI path lacks a security key, populate_db() at api_views/main.py:6 drops/recreates the database unauthenticated, and config.py has no global auth guard.]

Flask DEBUG Mode Enabled on All Interfaces — An attacker who triggers an unhandled exception can access the interactive Werkzeug debugger console and execute arbitrary Python code on the server, achieving remote code execution and full system compromise. [verified: Same code as findings 0 and 2 — debug=True is unconditionally enabled with host='0.0.0.0', making the Werkzeug interactive debugger and error-page information disclosure reachable from any network interface.]

Flask Debug Mode Enabled in Production with Unrestricted Host Binding — Remote code execution via Werkzeug debugger PIN, exposure of source code, environment variables, and stack traces. Combined with binding to 0.0.0.0 and lacking ALLOWED_HOSTS, the debugger is accessible from any network. [verified: Flask runs with debug=True hardcoded on a reachable path (if __name__=='__main__'), enabling Werkzeug debugger that leaks stack traces, environment variables, and local variables on any unhandled exception; RCE via the debugger console requires PIN bypass but information disclosure is immediate on all network interfaces.]

Passwords stored in plaintext in the database — If the database is compromised via SQL injection or direct file access, all user passwords are immediately exposed and can be reused on other services. [verified: Same plaintext storage as finding 1: the password column is a plain String(128) with no hashing at definition (line 15) or during __init__ assignment (line 24).]

Plaintext password storage — If the database is ever breached (via SQLi or file access), all user passwords are exposed in cleartext enabling credential stuffing and account takeover. [verified: Same plaintext storage as findings 1-2: password is a plain String column (line 15), assigned raw in __init__ (line 24), and compared directly in login_user() with == user.password; no hashing exists.]

Plaintext Password Storage — Any access to the database (via SQLi, debug endpoint, or direct file access) reveals all user passwords in plaintext, enabling full account takeover. Passwords are also exposed in API responses via the debug endpoint. [verified: Same plaintext storage as findings 1-2-5: password stored as plain String (line 15), assigned raw in __init__ (line 24); also exposed via unauthenticated json_debug() serialization (line 59) at the /users/v1/_debug endpoint.]

Plaintext Password Storage Without Hashing — All user passwords are stored in cleartext in the SQLite database, meaning any database compromise, SQL injection, or debug endpoint access directly exposes usable credentials for all accounts. [verified: password is stored as a plain db.Column(db.String(128)) at line 15 and assigned directly in __init__ at line 24; no hashing (bcrypt/PBKDF2/argon2) exists anywhere in the codebase.]

json_debug model method includes plaintext password in serialization — Any API endpoint that calls json_debug instead of json will inadvertently leak user passwords in its response. [verified: json_debug() at line 59 returns the plaintext password field and is called by the unauthenticated /users/v1/_debug endpoint (users.py:debug → get_all_users_debug), exposing all passwords with no auth requirement.]

Destructive Database Reset via HTTP GET Method — Database can be wiped via accidental browser prefetching, link previews, or CSRF-style attack if authentication is ever added to this endpoint [verified: The /createdb endpoint maps to populate_db() which calls db.drop_all() — a destructive operation — yet the OpenAPI spec defines it as an HTTP GET with no security requirement, allowing browser prefetch, link previews, or a simple tag on any webpage to trigger a full database wipe without user intent or authentication.]

Missing Rate Limiting on User Registration Endpoint — Attacker can programmatically create unlimited user accounts leading to database exhaustion, resource depletion, and enabling coordinated abuse [verified: No rate-limiting mechanism (Flask-Limiter, middleware, throttle config) exists anywhere in the codebase; the /users/v1/register endpoint (api_views/users.py:50) is unauthenticated per the OpenAPI spec and accepts unlimited requests with no counter in sight.]

Missing rate limiting enables brute-force on login endpoint — An attacker can brute-force user passwords without restriction, enabling account takeover especially when combined with user enumeration and the weak JWT signing secret. [verified: Duplicate of finding [4]: same missing rate-limiting on login endpoint at line 85, same absence of throttling/lockout throughout the codebase.]

User Enumeration via Distinct Login Error Messages — Attacker can compile a list of valid usernames through automated probing, dramatically reducing the search space for credential brute-force attacks. [verified: When vuln=1, login_user() returns distinct messages at lines 101-106: 'Password is not correct' vs 'Username does not exist'. No uniform-error control exists in vulnerable mode, enabling reliable username enumeration via response differentiation.]

ReDoS via catastrophic backtracking in email validation regex — An attacker can send a specially crafted email string that causes the regex engine to consume excessive CPU, resulting in denial of service. [verified: Duplicate of finding [5]: same ReDoS-vulnerable regex at line 144 in update_email(), same catastrophic backtracking on crafted email input.]

Password Change Without Current Password Verification — A stolen or forged JWT token allows an attacker to permanently change the victim's password without knowing the current one, enabling irreversible account takeover [verified: In the vuln=0 path at api_views/users.py:190-193, update_password authenticates via JWT but never validates the current password before setting user.password = request_data.get('password'); a stolen or forged token (trivial with SECRET_KEY='random') enables permanent account takeover with no old-password check.]
